NextItNet’s causal dilated convolutions provide concrete diagnostic invariants: changing future tokens must not change earlier features; perturbations outside a position’s computed receptive field must have no effect. Compute receptive fields from the actual convolution stack, including every convolution inside residual blocks. The original architecture and implementation establish these mechanisms ([NextItNet paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf), [implementation](https://recommenders-team.github.io/recommenders/_modules/recommenders/models/deeprec/models/sequential/nextitnet.html)). For this left-padded benchmark, explicitly test final-nonpadding readout against an injected count-minus-one bug. Padding invariance requires care: added padding can affect intermediate biased layers unless masking enforces equivalence.

Activation-patching research finds that corruption choices and evaluation metrics can materially change mechanistic conclusions ([ICLR 2024](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/06a52a54c8ee03cd86771136bc91eb1f-Abstract-Conference.html)). Suggested adaptation: compare each intervention with identity patches and matched random-position/layer controls on the same trained network and examples. Report paired score-margin and ranking changes; ablation damage alone does not establish a component-specific mechanism. Restore hooks and weights after each intervention.

Metamorphic testing and mutation testing support calibrating probes against deliberately introduced defects; a 2025 CNN study detected 85.71% of its injected implementation faults, a domain-specific result rather than an expected NextItNet detection rate ([study](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11888866/)). Proposed suite: isolated causality, dilation, padding and readout mutants; fault-specific detection rates, clean-model false-alarm rates, severity sweeps and uncertainty intervals. Distinguish structural violations from weak learned sensitivity: an in-field perturbation need not change predictions. In-memory feature/scoring consistency can be measured directly; checkpoint and generated-predictor reload parity remain unverified without a host execution interface.
